text: Scout's Eye. Explainable U19 match intelligence, built on Microsoft Foundry.
A U19 title decider. Northbridge need a draw, Vallora need a win. Second minute: goal. A fact card appears instantly, then the agents' verified commentary replaces it.
Same moment, two audiences. Fans get the story. Analysts get field tilt, PPDA and momentum, from the same verified facts, in English or Hungarian.
Click any overlay to see why it exists: the source events, the data, and the rule behind every claim. If the text says dominating, the numbers have to prove it.

Five agents work together in a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow. The Match Analyst decides what matters, Narrators write each version, and a Verifier checks every number, name and claim. Here the pre-check caught an unsupported claim and sent the text back for one repair.
Player focus: a fifteen-year-old full-back, still on the bench at thirty minutes, and the note says so. Low data, so no ranking claim. The model never knew who the planted talents were.
Forty-ninth minute: a Vallora penalty wins the title. The fact card comes first, then the verified text. The recap tells the story, and its numbers are checked against the match facts.
Synthetic data, checked against published U19 benchmarks. Five agents, one rule: never show a number you cannot prove. Scout's Eye. Try the live demo, link below.
